# Prompt 0 — Mission Context (send once at session start)

## Objective
You are about to build Proof of Reserve, Jac Enforced ("PoRJE"), a Jac-native protocol that turns a Chainlink Proof of Reserve attestation into an actionable permit — with a graph of claims, three independent approval walkers, an adversarial auditor, a locked printer, and a sized mint. This will be submitted to the Jack Hacks hackathon.

## The one-sentence thesis
Proof of Reserve attests that backing was reported. Proof of Reserve, Jac Enforced puts that attestation on a graph, requires three green stamps from walkers that are allowed to attack the claim, and only then mints — only as much as current coverage justifies — so "backed" is a permit with a quantity, not a text output you can quote.

## What the system does
A Chainlink PoR attestation and a price observation arrive. They are placed as typed nodes on a Jac graph alongside the asset, a child backing claim, and the protocol liability. Three approval walkers (Freshness, Cover, Auditor) each traverse the graph, write a Stamp node with a color (green / yellow / red / unknown) and reasons, and link it to the asset. Act is the only walker allowed to mint, and only if all three stamps are green. When it mints, it mints min(requested, justified_by_current_coverage) and writes a durable on-chain attestation record. Counsel narrates, but only after the stamps exist — it is blind until the graph is written.

## Architecture (ASCII)
Frontend (Next.js) → HTTP → Jac Cloud (jac start) → Ingest, Freshness, Cover, Auditor, Act, Counsel → Jac Graph (Asset, PriceObservation, ReserveAttestation, ChildClaim, Liability, Stamp, MintRecord) → EVM (Sepolia): Chainlink AggregatorV3 feeds, PoRToken (only Act may mint), PoRAttestation (ERC-721 durable record).

## Jac-native design principle
This is a Jac-native project, not a Python project with a Jac wrapper. Claims, observations, stamps, and records are node archetypes. Relationships are edge archetypes. Policy is enforced by walker archetypes with scoped abilities. The mint is a walker that reads other nodes and writes a new node. Python is used only as a thin bridge to web3.py for reading Chainlink feeds and writing EVM transactions.

## Build sequence
You will receive 13 numbered prompts. Execute them one at a time, in order. Do not proceed to the next prompt until every Acceptance Criterion of the current prompt passes.
Prompt 1 — Scaffold + root files. Prompt 2 — Jac schema, policy, colors, main.jac bootstrap. Prompt 3 — Chainlink bridge, fixtures, utils, fixtures loader. Prompt 4 — Solidity contracts, interfaces, deploy script. Prompt 5 — Ingest + Freshness walkers. Prompt 6 — Cover + Auditor walkers. Prompt 7 — Act walker + evm_py bridge + serialization. Prompt 8 — Counsel + DemoControl walkers. Prompt 9 — Backend wiring, read walkers, seed, run-demo CLI. Prompt 10 — Test suite + evm_spy + negative test enforcement. Prompt 11 — Frontend scaffold, types, jacClient, React Flow mapping. Prompt 12 — Frontend components + page.tsx. Prompt 13 — Docs + final three-path verification.

## Acknowledge
Before responding, confirm in one sentence that you understand the mission and the build sequence. Then wait for Prompt 1.

# Prompt 1 — Scaffold & Root Files ## Objective Create the full directory tree and every root-level file for the proof-of-reserve-jac project. Populate only the files that are safe to fully populate now (README, demo.md, configs). Leave all logic-bearing files as language-appropriate stubs with header comments. ## Prerequisites Prompt 0 acknowledged. ## Directory tree to create proof-of-reserve-jac/ with: README.md, demo.md, LICENSE, .gitignore, .env.example, jac.toml, requirements.txt, package.json; docs/ (architecture.md, policy.md, walkers.md, demo-runbook.md); jac/ (main.jac; schemas/nodes.jac, schemas/edges.jac; walkers/ingest.jac, freshness.jac, cover.jac, auditor.jac, act.jac, counsel.jac, demo_control.jac; lib/policy.jac, colors.jac, chainlink.jac, chainlink_py.py, evm_py.py, fixtures.jac, utils.jac; tests/test_freshness.jac, test_cover.jac, test_auditor.jac, test_act.jac, test_paths.jac, evm_spy.py); contracts/ (PoRToken.sol, PoRAttestation.sol, interfaces/AggregatorV3Interface.sol, interfaces/IPoRToken.sol); scripts/ (deploy_contracts.py, seed_graph.py, run_demo_path.py); frontend/ (package.json, next.config.js, tsconfig.json, tailwind.config.js, postcss.config.js, public/logo.svg, src/app/layout.tsx, src/app/page.tsx, src/app/globals.css, src/components/GraphView.tsx, StampBadge.tsx, MintButton.tsx, AuditorPanel.tsx, CounselPanel.tsx, PathSelector.tsx, ExplorerLink.tsx, PolicyCard.tsx, src/lib/jacClient.ts, types.ts, constants.ts, src/styles/.gitkeep); fixtures/ (por_live.json, por_stale.json, por_flat.json, price_live.json, price_stale.json, child_missing.json, child_stale.json). ## README.md — write verbatim # Proof of Reserve, Jac Enforced **PoR attests. Jac enforces. The printer is the proof.** Proof of Reserve, Jac Enforced is a Jac protocol that takes a Chainlink Proof of Reserve attestation and turns it into something a system can actually use: a graph of claims, three independent approvals, and a mint that is allowed only when all three are green — and only in the amount current coverage justifies. This is not an oracle project. It does not replace Chainlink Proof of Reserve. PoR remains the attestation: backing was reported. This product is the runtime that decides whether that attestation is still actionable, and then either prints the asset or refuses in public. ## The problem Chainlink Proof of Reserve already does the hard job. It publishes that, at a given time, an attested reserve amount existed for an asset. That output is a fact. In practice most applications treat it as a badge. A reserve number is read and shown. Nothing has to happen because of it. A price can be live while the reserve attestation is old; both screens can still look fine. A reserve feed can keep posting a new timestamp while the amount never moves as the market does — a heartbeat with no pulse. Backing is often a chain of claims: this asset is backed by that, and that is itself a claim. A missing or stale child still leaves the parent looking attested. Vaults, mints, collateral listings, and basket legs inherit "backed" without walking what sits underneath. Missing Proof of Reserve is usually an empty field, not a hard stop. So PoR today is strong as an attestation and weak as a protocol primitive. It is text (or a feed) you can point at. It is not a door you have to pass through, and it does not decide how much may be printed. ## The solution Keep Chainlink's attestation as the sensor. Add a Jac workflow that the attestation must survive before money can be printed. The object of the system is not a row in a table. It is a graph of claims: the asset whose printer we control; a price observation (value + time + live vs fixture); a reserve attestation (amount + time + live vs fixture); at least one child claim when the reserve itself depends on something else; and dependents that would inherit this asset's "backed" status if we let them. Walkers move across that graph. Each walker has one job. None of the first three may mint. The mint walker is locked until three stamps are green. When it mints, it does not mint a souvenir amount. It mints what current coverage justifies, and it leaves an on-chain record of why. PoR attests. Jac enforces. The printer is the proof. ## Why better than PoR alone PoR alone: publishes a reserve at a time; display/integration snippet; one asset one number; freshness optional; no stuck-but-punctual reserve; missing feed is empty UI; you write your own adapter. PoRJE: decides if actionable; a workflow ending in mint or visible refuse; a backing graph (parent, child, dependents); freshness is a stamp; unchanged reserve while price moved is a finding; missing PoR is unknown; the permit, size, refuse, and explanation are the product. ## Why an exceptional use of Jac Jaseci's point is data and compute are the same graph. Claims are nodes. Walkers have one authority each (Freshness looks at clocks; Cover computes coverage; Auditor attacks; Act is the only spender; Counsel is a mouth). Verdicts are written onto the graph, not held in a chat. The explainer is blind until writes exist. The only spender is a walker that reads the stamps. You do not glue a dashboard to a bot. You walk an attestation until it is allowed to print. ## Why Chainlink Proof of Reserve PoR is the sensor. It already publishes attested reserve amounts. This project does not replace it — it makes it actionable. The PoR feed is read directly through AggregatorV3Interface; fixtures are labeled as fixtures and never costumed as live. ## Demo See demo.md for the exact three-path demonstration and operator runbook. ## Repository layout jac/ — Jac Cloud project. contracts/ — PoRToken (mint locked to Act) and PoRAttestation. frontend/ — Next.js demo surface. fixtures/ — schema-faithful JSON inputs. ## License MIT. ## demo.md — write verbatim # Demo — Proof of Reserve, Jac Enforced Audience: Jack Hacks judges. Length: 4 minutes live + 1 minute Q&A. Surface: Next.js frontend at http://localhost:3000 + Etherscan tabs pre-opened. ## Pre-demo checklist (run 10 minutes before) 1. jac start jac/main.jac is running and /health returns 200. 2. cd frontend && npm run dev is running. 3. .env has POR_TOKEN_ADDRESS, POR_ATTESTATION_ADDRESS, PRICE_FEED_ADDRESS, RESERVE_FEED_ADDRESS, SEPOLIA_RPC_URL. 4. Two browser tabs pre-opened: demo UI and https://sepolia.etherscan.io/address/$POR_TOKEN_ADDRESS. 5. A wallet with Sepolia ETH unlocked for the deployer. 6. No fixture has label != "fixture". ## The screen In order: Header (asset symbol, chain, token address truncated); PolicyCard (active POLICY values); GraphView (nodes and edges of the claim graph; price and reserve labeled live or fixture); StampBadge row (Freshness, Cover, Auditor); AuditorPanel (verbatim finding lines); CounselPanel (narration, disabled until three stamps exist); PathSelector (Happy, Yellow, Unknown); MintButton (disabled unless three greens; shows justified_amount); ExplorerLink (after successful mint). ## Path 1 — Happy (all green) 1. Click Happy. DemoControl seeds live-shaped fixtures. 2. Click Freshness. Badge green. Reasons appear. 3. Click Cover. Badge green. "coverage ratio 1.25 ≥ 1.0", "justified amount: 250,000 pUSD". 4. Click Auditor. Badge green. All four checklist lines appear even on pass. 5. Enter requested_amount = 1000000. Click Act. 6. UI shows minted: 250,000 pUSD. Not 1,000,000. 7. Click Counsel. Narrates. 8. Open Etherscan tx. ## Path 2 — Yellow (stale or stuck reserve) 1. Click Yellow. DemoControl seeds a flat reserve. 2. Run Freshness → Cover → Auditor. 3. Cover yellow: "flat reserve while price moved (punctual but no pulse)". 4. Click Act. Refuses. 5. Click Counsel. Speaks. ## Path 3 — Unknown / red (missing PoR or missing child) 1. Click Unknown. DemoControl drops the child attestation. 2. Run Freshness → Cover → Auditor. 3. Freshness unknown. Cover red. Auditor red. 4. Click Act. Refuses. 5. Click Counsel. Names the hole. ## Why this is an impressive use of Jac's capabilities "In Jac, data and compute are the same graph. Here, the claims are nodes, the walkers are the compute, the stamps are the verdicts, and the mint is a walker that reads the verdicts. We did not build a dashboard that queries a database. We built a graph that carries its own policy, its own auditors, and its own printer." Concretely: (1) Graph-native policy — approvals are Stamp nodes on the Asset. (2) Walker-scoped authority — Act is the only walker imported into the EVM bridge. (3) Blind explainer — Counsel refuses to speak until three stamps exist. (4) Adversarial visibility — Auditor writes findings even on green. (5) Sized printing — mint = min(requested, justified_by_coverage). (6) Durable on-chain record — PoRAttestation stores stamps, times, coverage. ## Post-demo pointer Open docs/architecture.md and docs/policy.md. Both fit on one screen. ## LICENSE MIT, year 2025, holder PoRJE Contributors. ## .gitignore .venv/ __pycache__/ *.pyc node_modules/ .next/ out/ cache/ artifacts/ .env *.log .DS_Store jac-cloud-state/ dist/ build/ ## .env.example SEPOLIA_RPC_URL= DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY= POR_TOKEN_ADDRESS= POR_ATTESTATION_ADDRESS= PRICE_FEED_ADDRESS= RESERVE_FEED_ADDRESS= JAC_CLOUD_URL=http://localhost:8000 CHAIN_ID=11155111 NEXT_PUBLIC_JAC_URL=http://localhost:8000 ## jac.toml [project] name = "por-jac-enforced" version = "0.1.0" description = "Proof of Reserve, Jac Enforced — a Jac-native PoR enforcement protocol" [server] host = "0.0.0.0" port = 8000 ## requirements.txt jaclang>=0.7.0 jaseci>=0.7.0 web3>=6.0.0 python-dotenv eth-account requests pytest ## package.json (root) {"name":"por-jac-enforced","version":"0.1.0","private":true,"scripts":{"deploy":"python scripts/deploy_contracts.py","seed":"python scripts/seed_graph.py","jac:serve":"jac start jac/main.jac","frontend:dev":"cd frontend && npm run dev"}} ## Stub files Every file not listed above gets a header comment block: "# / # Purpose: / # Owner walker/module: / # Spec: see PRD §
/ # Status: SCAFFOLD — no logic implemented" (use // for Solidity/TS). Then a language-appropriate stub: jac/schemas/*.jac header only + TODO; jac/lib/policy.jac and colors.jac header + TODO; jac/main.jac header + with entry { print("PoRJE scaffold booted"); }; all jac/walkers/*.jac header only + TODO; jac/lib/{chainlink.jac, chainlink_py.py, evm_py.py, fixtures.jac, utils.jac} header + empty signatures; jac/tests/*.jac header + empty test block; evm_spy.py header + empty module; contracts/*.sol header + TODO; scripts/*.py header + print + TODO; docs/*.md header + heading outline + TODO; frontend/package.json minimal Next.js 14 + React 18 + TS + Tailwind + reactflow; next.config.js module.exports = { reactStrictMode: true }; tsconfig.json standard with paths; tailwind.config.js content globs; postcss.config.js tailwindcss+autoprefixer; public/logo.svg one-line placeholder; layout.tsx imports globals.css renders children; page.tsx placeholder
PoRJE
; globals.css Tailwind directives; all components return
{name}
; lib/{types,jacClient,constants}.ts empty exports; styles/.gitkeep empty; all fixtures/*.json with "label":"fixture" and "TODO" field. ## Agent Grounding Do NOT install dependencies. Do NOT run npm install, pip install, jac, hardhat. Scaffolding only. Do NOT create a git commit. Do NOT add files not listed. README and demo.md must be full content, not summaries. ## Acceptance Criteria 1. find . -type f ... returns every path listed. 2. README.md and demo.md match verbatim. 3. Every non-populated file has the header comment. 4. No file contains implemented business logic for any walker. ## Do NOT Do not install dependencies. Do not run builds. Do not implement any walker, contract, script, or component logic. Do not add files beyond the tree.

# Prompt 3 — Chainlink Bridge, Fixtures, Utils, Fixtures Loader

## Objective
Populate the Chainlink integration layer, utils, fixtures loader, and all seven fixture JSON files. Fixtures are schema-faithful and labeled; no code path may produce source="live" from a fixture.

## Prerequisites
Prompt 2 complete.

## jac/lib/chainlink_py.py
from web3 import Web3; import os; import json. Load ABI from contracts/interfaces/AggregatorV3Interface.json. def _w3(): return Web3(Web3.HTTPProvider(os.environ["SEPOLIA_RPC_URL"])). def latest_round(feed_address: str) -> dict: create contract with Web3.to_checksum_address; call latestRoundData() and decimals(); return dict with round_id (int), answer (float = raw / 10**decimals), started_at (int), updated_at (int), answered_in_round (int), feed_address (str), decimals (int). All return values cast to primitives.

## jac/lib/chainlink.jac
import from chainlink_py { latest_round } can fetch(feed: str) -> dict { return latest_round(feed); }

## jac/lib/utils.jac
import time; can now_unix() -> int { return int(time.time()); } can abs_diff(a: float, b: float) -> float { if a > b { return a - b; } return b - a; } can pct_change(old: float, new: float) -> float { if old == 0.0 { return 0.0; } return (new - old) / old; }

## jac/lib/fixtures.jac
import json; import os; import from utils { now_unix } glob FIXTURES_DIR = <path to fixtures/>; can load_fixture(name: str) -> dict { path = os.path.join(FIXTURES_DIR, name + ".json"); open, json.load; assert raw["label"] == "fixture"; raw["source"] = "fixture"; raw["timestamp"] = now_unix() + int(raw.get("timestamp_offset_seconds", 0)); return raw; }

## Fixtures — every file has "label": "fixture"
por_live.json: {label, amount:1250000.0, timestamp_offset_seconds:-30, feed_address:"0x0...", round_id:1001, answered_in_round:1001, provenance:"fixtures/por_live.json"}
por_stale.json: amount:1250000.0, timestamp_offset_seconds:-7200
por_flat.json: amount:1250000.0, timestamp_offset_seconds:-30, extra "flat_history":[1250000.0,1250000.0,1250000.0]
price_live.json: value:1.0002, timestamp_offset_seconds:-12, feed_address, round_id:2001, provenance
price_stale.json: value:0.9800, timestamp_offset_seconds:-900
child_missing.json: asset_id:"USDC", amount:0.0, timestamp_offset_seconds:-30, present:false, provenance
child_stale.json: asset_id:"USDC", amount:1250000.0, timestamp_offset_seconds:-7200, present:true

## Agent Grounding
Python files imported from Jac with import from chainlink_py { latest_round }. The .py file must be in the same directory as the .jac file or on sys.path. json, os, time importable in Jac. assert keyword available. Do not pass Jac node instances across the Python boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Every fixture has "label":"fixture". 2. load_fixture("por_live") returns source=="fixture" and timestamp close to now_unix()-30. 3. load_fixture("child_missing") returns present==false. 4. No file in jac/lib/ other than chainlink_py.py imports web3 directly.

## Do NOT
Do not implement any walker. Do not add a code path where a fixture can produce source="live". Do not read real feeds here (only the wrapper).

# Prompt 4 — Solidity Contracts, Interfaces, Deploy Script

## Objective
Populate PoRToken.sol, PoRAttestation.sol, both interfaces, and the deploy script. PoRToken.mint is callable only by the address the owner sets as actWalker.

## Prerequisites
Prompt 3 complete.

## contracts/interfaces/AggregatorV3Interface.sol
pragma solidity ^0.8.20; interface AggregatorV3Interface { function decimals() external view returns (uint8); function description() external view returns (string memory); function version() external view returns (uint256); function getRoundData(uint80 _roundId) external view returns (uint80, int256, uint256, uint256, uint80); function latestRoundData() external view returns (uint80, int256, uint256, uint256, uint80); }

## contracts/interfaces/AggregatorV3Interface.json
Standard ABI for latestRoundData, decimals, description, version, getRoundData.

## contracts/interfaces/IPoRToken.sol
interface IPoRToken { function mint(address to, uint256 amount, string calldata reason) external; }

## contracts/PoRToken.sol — write verbatim
pragma solidity ^0.8.20; imports ERC20 and Ownable. contract PoRToken is ERC20, Ownable { address public actWalker; event Minted(address indexed to, uint256 amount, string reason); modifier onlyAct() { require(msg.sender == actWalker, "PoRToken: caller is not Act"); _; } constructor(string memory name_, string memory symbol_) ERC20(name_, symbol_) Ownable(msg.sender) {} function setActWalker(address _walker) external onlyOwner { actWalker = _walker; } function mint(address to, uint256 amount, string calldata reason) external onlyAct { _mint(to, amount); emit Minted(to, amount, reason); } }

## contracts/PoRAttestation.sol — write verbatim
pragma solidity ^0.8.20; imports ERC721 and Ownable. contract PoRAttestation is ERC721, Ownable { uint256 private _nextId; struct Record { uint256 mintedAmount; uint256 coverageUsed; uint256 priceTime; uint256 reserveTime; string stampSummary; } mapping(uint256 => Record) public records; event AttestationMinted(uint256 indexed tokenId, uint256 mintedAmount, string stampSummary); constructor() ERC721("PoR Attestation", "PoRATT") Ownable(msg.sender) {} function mintAttestation(address to, uint256 mintedAmount, uint256 coverageUsed, uint256 priceTime, uint256 reserveTime, string calldata stampSummary) external onlyOwner returns (uint256) { uint256 id = ++_nextId; _safeMint(to, id); records[id] = Record(mintedAmount, coverageUsed, priceTime, reserveTime, stampSummary); emit AttestationMinted(id, mintedAmount, stampSummary); return id; } }

## scripts/deploy_contracts.py
Load .env. Create Web3 with SEPOLIA_RPC_URL. Account.from_key(DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY). Load prebuilt artifacts from artifacts/PoRToken.json and artifacts/PoRAttestation.json. Deploy both. Call setActWalker(deployer). Append POR_TOKEN_ADDRESS and POR_ATTESTATION_ADDRESS to .env. Print Etherscan links.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Contracts compile with OpenZeppelin v5, solc 0.8.20+. 2. PoRToken.mint is onlyAct; actWalker set by onlyOwner. 3. PoRAttestation.mintAttestation is onlyOwner; emits AttestationMinted with stampSummary. 4. deploy_contracts.py writes both addresses to .env and prints Etherscan links. 5. No public mint on PoRToken.

## Do NOT
Do not add a public mint. Do not add mintAttestation callable by arbitrary addresses. Do not add cross-chain logic. Single chain only.

# Prompt 5 — Ingest + Freshness Walkers

## Objective
Implement Ingest (loads facts onto the graph) and Freshness (looks at clocks only, writes a color stamp). Both fail closed: missing inputs → unknown.

## Prerequisites
Prompt 4 complete.

## jac/walkers/ingest.jac
walker:pub Ingest with has fields price_feed_address, reserve_feed_address, child_asset_id, use_fixture, fixture_name. Ability: can ingest with Asset entry. Logic: if use_fixture: price_data = load_fixture("price_" + fixture_name.split("_")[0]); reserve_data = load_fixture(fixture_name). Else: if either feed address empty → report {"error":"feed_addresses_missing"}. Fetch both via chainlink.fetch; set source="live", provenance=feed, value/amount=answer, timestamp=updated_at. If either missing → report {"error":"feed_unavailable"}. Detach any existing HasPrice/HasReserve/HasLiability edges. Create PriceObservation, ReserveAttestation, ChildClaim (from load_fixture("child_"+stem)), Liability (minted_units=1000000.0, demo_position=1000000.0). Wire with here +>: HasPrice() :+> price_node; etc., and reserve_node +>: DependsOn() :+> child_node. Report {"asset_id": here.id, "price_source": price_node.source, "reserve_source": reserve_node.source}.

## jac/walkers/freshness.jac
walker:pub Freshness { can run with Asset entry { now = now_unix(); prices = [here ->:HasPrice:->]; reserves = [here ->:HasReserve:->]; if len(prices)==0 or len(reserves)==0 → color=COLOR_UNKNOWN, reasons=["missing price observation"/"missing reserve observation"]. Else: p_age = now - price.timestamp; r_age = now - reserve.timestamp; max_p = POLICY["max_price_age_seconds"]; max_r = POLICY["max_reserve_age_seconds"]; if p_age > max_p → min_color(color, COLOR_RED), reason. Else reason "price age Ns ≤ max". if r_age > max_r → min_color(color, COLOR_RED); elif r_age > int(max_r * 0.5) → min_color(color, COLOR_YELLOW); else reason. If price.source=="fixture" or reserve.source=="fixture" → append "source is fixture (labeled)". Remove prior Freshness stamp if any. Create Stamp(walker_name="Freshness", color, reasons, timestamp=now, payload={}) and wire here +>: StampedBy() :+> stamp. Report {"walker":"Freshness", "color":color, "reasons":reasons}. } }

Add to main.jac: import from walkers.ingest { Ingest } and import from walkers.freshness { Freshness }.

## Agent Grounding
Forward traversal by typed edge: [here ->:HasPrice:->]. Typed edge creation: here +>: HasPrice() :+> node;. Detach: detach here :HasPrice: old;. walker:pub Name { ... } exposes POST /walker/Name. report sends the dict. here is current node inside walker ability. self is walker instance. Do NOT use -[HasPrice]->, -->:HasPrice:-->, or visit syntax.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Ingest with use_fixture=True, fixture_name="por_live" creates PriceObservation, ReserveAttestation with DependsOn child, and Liability. 2. Every fixture-created node has source="fixture". 3. Freshness with fresh price + reserve writes a single Stamp(walker_name="Freshness", color="green"). 4. Freshness with missing price writes Stamp(color="unknown") with reason "missing price observation". 5. Freshness does not import or reference Act, Cover, or Auditor.

## Do NOT
Do not let Freshness compute coverage, flatness, or child status. Do not let Freshness mint. Do not let Freshness write more than one Freshness stamp per asset.

# Prompt 6 — Cover + Auditor Walkers

## Objective
Implement Cover (coverage + justified amount) and Auditor (adversarial findings even on green).

## Prerequisites
Prompt 5 complete.

## jac/walkers/cover.jac
walker:pub Cover { can run with Asset entry { now = now_unix(); prices = [here ->:HasPrice:->]; reserves = [here ->:HasReserve:->]; liabs = [here ->:HasLiability:->]; color=COLOR_GREEN; reasons=[]; justified=0.0; ratio=0.0; if any missing → COLOR_UNKNOWN, reason "missing price, reserve, or liability". Else: children = [reserve ->:DependsOn:->]; if len==0 or children[0].present==false → min_color(color, COLOR_RED), "child attestation: missing"; elif (now - children[0].timestamp) > POLICY["child_max_age_seconds"] → min_color(color, COLOR_RED), "child attestation: stale"; else "child attestation: present". Flat reserve check: if reserve.amount > 0.0: hist = reserve.flat_history if hasattr(reserve, "flat_history") else []; if len(hist) >= POLICY["flat_reserve_windows"]: amount_stable = abs_diff(hist[0], hist[-1]) / hist[0] < POLICY["flat_reserve_epsilon"]; if amount_stable → min_color(color, COLOR_YELLOW), "flat reserve while price moved (punctual but no pulse)". Coverage: coverage_value = reserve.amount * price.value; liability_value = (liab.minted_units + liab.demo_position) * price.value; ratio = coverage_value / liability_value if liability_value > 0.0 else 0.0. If ratio < coverage_floor_ratio → COLOR_RED. elif ratio < min_coverage_ratio → COLOR_YELLOW. else reason "coverage ratio N ≥ min". Justified: max_mintable = (coverage_value / price.value) - liab.minted_units - liab.demo_position; justified = max_mintable if > 0.0 else 0.0; append "justified amount: N". Remove prior Cover stamp. Create Stamp(walker_name="Cover", color, reasons, timestamp=now, payload={"justified_amount": justified, "coverage_ratio": ratio}). Report {"walker":"Cover", "color":color, "reasons":reasons, "justified_amount":justified, "coverage_ratio":ratio}. } }

## jac/walkers/auditor.jac
walker:pub Auditor { can run with Asset entry { now = now_unix(); prices = [here ->:HasPrice:->]; reserves = [here ->:HasReserve:->]; liabs = [here ->:HasLiability:->]; color=COLOR_GREEN; findings=[]. If price or reserve missing → COLOR_UNKNOWN, findings: "age skew — unknown (missing price or reserve)", "flat reserve — unknown", "child attestation — unknown", "liability cover — unknown". Else: 1. Age skew: skew = abs_diff(price.timestamp, reserve.timestamp); if skew > max_price_age → COLOR_RED, "age skew — Ns exceeds Ms"; else "age skew — none". 2. Flat reserve: hist = reserve.flat_history if hasattr else []; if len>=flat_windows and abs_diff(hist[0],hist[-1])/hist[0] < flat_eps → COLOR_YELLOW, "flat reserve — unchanged across windows while price moved"; else "flat reserve — none". 3. Child: children = [reserve ->:DependsOn:->]; missing → RED, "child attestation — missing"; stale → RED, "child attestation — stale"; else "child attestation — present". 4. Liability cover: ratio = coverage/liability; < floor → RED, "liability cover — fails"; < min → YELLOW, "liability cover — thin"; else "liability cover — holds". Remove prior Auditor stamp. Create Stamp(walker_name="Auditor", color, reasons=findings, timestamp=now, payload={}). Report {"walker":"Auditor", "color":color, "reasons":findings}. } }

## Prerequisites
Prompt 12 complete.

## docs/architecture.md
Sections: Overview, Component Diagram, Data Flow, Invariants, Testability. Overview: the thesis sentence and a one-paragraph description. Component Diagram: paste the ASCII diagram from Prompt 0. Data Flow: Ingest → Freshness → Cover → Auditor → Act → Counsel; note Counsel is blind until stamps exist. Invariants: (1) Jac graph is single source of truth. (2) Only Act calls evm_py. (3) Only three approval walkers: Freshness, Cover, Auditor. (4) Missing stamp is not green. (5) Missing fixture label is a boot error. (6) min(requested, justified) is the mint rule. Testability: explain evm_spy mechanism and why Act imports evm_py as a module (so spy can monkey-patch the module attribute). This is the only place the spy mechanism is documented.

## Final Acceptance Criteria — confirm and paste evidence
1. jac start jac/main.jac boots with no errors. 2. All walkers reachable at POST /walker/{Name}: Ingest, Freshness, Cover, Auditor, Act, Counsel, DemoControl, GetAsset, GetStamps, SeedAsset. 3. SeedAsset creates root Asset with token address from .env. 4. DemoControl happy → three green stamps; Act mints min(requested, justified) and writes MintRecord. 5. DemoControl yellow → Cover yellow; Act refuses; no MintRecord. 6. DemoControl unknown → Freshness unknown, Cover red, Auditor red; Act refuses; no MintRecord. 7. jac test jac/tests/ passes including spy-based negative tests. 8. Counsel returns {"spoken": false} before three stamps and {"spoken": true} after. 9. Every fixture has "label":"fixture". 10. No file other than act.jac imports evm_py. 11. frontend/ builds with npm run build. 12. README.md and demo.md are exact content from Prompt 1. 13. docs/*.md are populated and complete. 14. The one-sentence thesis appears verbatim in README.md, demo.md, and docs/architecture.md: Proof of Reserve attests that backing was reported. Proof of Reserve, Jac Enforced puts that attestation on a graph, requires three green stamps from walkers that are allowed to attack the claim, and only then mints — only as much as current coverage justifies — so "backed" is a permit with a quantity, not a text output you can quote.
